**Overview of the DogeOS “Heist” Testnet** [SRC-4c0c1616bd72]

**Purpose**
Heist is presented as a *crew‑based discovery and engagement layer* for Dogecoin‑focused dApps. [SRC-4c0c1616bd72]
It groups ecosystem projects into “crews” that publish missions for users to complete, helping participants learn what each app is building and earn rewards [SRC-4c0c1616bd72].

**Relation to the DogeOS Testnet** [SRC-202a151d100e]
The available documentation describes the DogeOS “Chikyū” testnet, which provides RPC endpoints, a faucet, and tooling for deploying smart contracts [SRC-202a151d100e].
Heist is accessed via the separate web UI at heist.dogeos.com and does not appear to be a distinct blockchain network; rather, it operates on top of the existing DogeOS testnet infrastructure (unverified: no matching retrieved evidence).
The Grand Heist site shows the UI/mission experience (factions, decrypt challenges, etc.) but gives no network‑level details (unverified: no matching retrieved evidence).

**Launch Date and Current Status** (unverified: no matching retrieved evidence).
Heist went live on **May 9, 2026** at heist.dogeos.com, announced by the official DogeOS account [SRC-4c0c1616bd72].
At launch eight crews were active (e.g., USDoge, Metafide, DerpsParty). [SRC-4c0c1616bd72]
The site continues to list active crews, missions, and a community Discord, indicating that the platform remains operational, though no real‑time status metrics are provided in the sources (unverified: no matching retrieved evidence).

**Technical Specifications**
- **Consensus / Chain ID**: Not disclosed; Heist appears to rely on the underlying DogeOS Chikyū testnet, whose consensus details are not detailed in the retrieved sources (unverified: no matching retrieved evidence).
- **Block Time / RPC Endpoints**: Not mentioned for Heist; developers are directed to the generic DogeOS testnet guides for RPC configuration (unverified: no matching retrieved evidence).
- **Token Economics**: Missions reward participants with testnet DOGE, but exact reward amounts, supply caps, or faucet limits for Heist‑specific missions are not provided (unverified: no matching retrieved evidence).
The Chikyū testnet faucet supplies DOGE for general testing [SRC-f69daf6c874a].
- **Faucet Availability**: A faucet exists for the DogeOS Chikyū testnet () [SRC-f69daf6c874a]; there is no dedicated Heist faucet mentioned.

**How to Participate**
1.
**Join the community** – Connect via the Discord link on the Heist site [SRC-6148010135ac].
2.
**Get testnet DOGE** – Use the Chikyū testnet faucet to obtain DOGE for transactions [SRC-f69daf6c874a].
3.
**Access the Heist UI** – Visit https://heist.dogeos.com and select a crew or mission (unverified: no matching retrieved evidence).
4.
**Complete missions** – Follow on‑screen instructions (e.g., Decrypt Protocol challenges) to earn rewards (unverified: no matching retrieved evidence).
5.
**Deploy contracts (optional)** – Use DogeOS developer guides to compile and deploy contracts to the Chikyū testnet, then interact with them via Heist missions [SRC-202a151d100e].

**Key Takeaways**
- Heist is a discovery/mission layer launched May 9 2026, not a separate blockchain network. [SRC-4c0c1616bd72]
- It runs on the DogeOS Chikyū testnet, leveraging the same faucet and RPC infrastructure (unverified: no matching retrieved evidence).
- Detailed technical parameters (consensus, block time, reward formulas) are not disclosed in the available sources (unverified: no matching retrieved evidence).

Home / News / DogeOS Launches Heist, a Crew-Based Discovery Layer for Dogecoin Apps
TL;DR
DogeOS, the application layer for Dogecoin built by the team behind MyDoge wallet, has launched Heist at heist.dogeos.com. The platform organizes ecosystem apps into crews that publish missions for the community to complete. Eight crews are live in the Heist room at launch, with more rolling out.
Heist went live at heist.dogeos.com on May 9, 2026, announced from the @DogeOS account
Apps in the Heist room are organized as crews that post missions for users to complete and learn what each project is building
Featured launch crews include USDoge, Metafide, DerpsParty, Doge Museum, ItPlaysOut, MuchFi, MOAR HQ, and BarkSwap
DogeOS raised $6.9 million in May 2025, led by Polychain Capital, to build the Dogecoin app layer
The platform is built by the team behind MyDoge, which lists more than half a million users on its wallet

DogeOS is built by the team behind MyDoge, the largest Dogecoin wallet by user count
The platform raised $6.9 million in funding led by Polychain Capital in May 2025 to build out the app layer
Heist is positioned as a discovery and engagement layer rather than a single app, with missions designed to surface what each crew is shipping
DogeOS, the application layer aiming to bring smart contracts, gaming, and consumer dApps to the Dogecoin ecosystem, has switched on a new product called Heist. "The first signal is live," DogeOS posted on May 9, pointing users to heist.dogeos.com and listing the launch crews already mobilizing inside the Heist room. source The framing is deliberate: Heist is a coordination layer, not a single dApp, where projects building on DogeOS surface their products to the community through missions.
What Heist Actually Is
Strip away the heist metaphor and the product is recognizable as a quest hub. Apps signed up to the platform appear as crews. Each crew posts missions that users can complete, and the missions double as guided tours of what those projects do.
The eight crews featured at launch span several categories of the Dogecoin app layer. USDoge is a Dogecoin-pegged stable asset effort. Metafide is an AI-driven crypto prediction product the DogeOS team has flagged as a key ecosystem integration. DerpsParty leans social and meme-native. Doge Museum points at culture and collectibles. ItPlaysOut, MuchFi, MOAR HQ, and BarkSwap fill out the early roster across gaming, DeFi, and exchange surfaces.

evidenceSnippets: To interact with our testnet, you can request DOGE directly on the DogeOS Testnet , or you can try our bridge demo app (advanced users only).
If you don’t want to interact with the bridge, our faucet directly distributes DogeOS Chikyū Testnet DOGE.

To interact with our testnet, you can request DOGE directly on the DogeOS Testnet , or you can try our bridge demo app (advanced users only).
DogeOS Chikyū Testnet Faucets #
If you don’t want to interact with the bridge, our faucet directly distributes DogeOS Chikyū Testnet DOGE.
https://faucet.testnet.dogeos.com
Once you claim DOGE on DogeOS Testnet , you should see it in your wallet within a few seconds. View your DogeOS wallet on our DogeOS Chikyū Testnet Block Explorer .
Dogecoin Testnet Faucets #
If you are an advanced user and want to try out the bridge, you can request DOGE on the Dogecoin Testnet.
Note that using the bridge requires you to be able to send a transaction including OP_RETURN data.
https://faucet.dogetest.doge.xyz
Once you claim DOGE on Dogecoin Testnet , you should see it in your wallet within a few minutes. View your Dogecoin wallet on the Dogecoin Testnet Explorer .
